item.title: GitHub OAuth to GitHub App
item.description:
Use this runbook to move a GitHub OAuth org (gh/…) to a standalone GitHub App org (circleci/…). Do the prep ahead of time, including the support requests, then run the cutover inside a freeze window.

At a glance 

flowchart LR
subgraph prep ["Prep (days before)"]
direction TB
A["Doctor, export"] --> B["mapping.json,<br/>secrets context"] --> C["Dry runs"]
end
subgraph before ["Cutover: source still live"]
direction TB
D["Freeze merges,<br/>create projects"] --> E["Transfer secrets"] --> F["Pause source"]
end
subgraph after ["Cutover: destination"]
direction TB
H["Add pipelines<br/>and triggers"] --> I["Plan, orbs, runners"] --> J["Enable destination"] --> K["Smoke test, validate"]
end
prep --> before --> G["Move GitHub App<br/>POINT OF NO RETURN"] --> after
classDef ponr fill:#b42318,stroke:#7a1a12,stroke-width:2px,color:#fff
class G ponr

Order matters: move secrets while the source can still build, and pause the source before the App moves.

What moves

  • Moves automatically: contexts, projects, project and org settings, project and expression context restrictions, pipeline definitions and triggers (created disabled).
  • Needs a step: secret values, webhook secrets and URLs, the plan and any orb namespace (CircleCI support).
  • Not carried over: fork-PR builds, fork-PR secrets, the OSS flag and pr_only_branch_overrides have no App equivalent. Use trigger filters in the pipeline definition, and tell contributors.
  • Group context restrictions resolve by group name if the group exists in the destination. Otherwise they become manual: use expression or project restrictions.
  • Each OAuth project without an App definition gets one synthesized build-and-test definition. Add other config paths by hand. Trigger names are assigned by CircleCI, not copied.
  • SSO, build history and Insights do not move.

The full list is in what moves. This migration is lossy, so read it before you start.

Before you start

  • You are an admin of both CircleCI orgs and can install and uninstall the CircleCI GitHub App in the GitHub org.
  • The destination org exists. You have its Organization ID (Organization Settings > Overview) and a personal API token for each org (User Settings > Personal API Tokens).
  • A GitHub token with repo read. Any OAuth project without a captured GitHub App pipeline needs it to look up the repo ID, and preflight fails without it.
  • The CLI is installed (install). circleci-migrate version prints v0.19.0 or later.

Set up 

export SOURCE_ORG="gh/acme"
export DEST_ORG="circleci/<dest-org-id>"
export DEST_ORG_ID="<dest-org-uuid>"
export CIRCLECI_SOURCE_TOKEN="<source-org-admin-token>"
export CIRCLECI_DEST_TOKEN="<destination-org-admin-token>"
export GITHUB_TOKEN="<github-pat-with-repo-read>"
$SOURCE_ORG = "gh/acme"
$DEST_ORG = "circleci/<dest-org-id>"
$DEST_ORG_ID = "<dest-org-uuid>"
$env:CIRCLECI_SOURCE_TOKEN = "<source-org-admin-token>"
$env:CIRCLECI_DEST_TOKEN = "<destination-org-admin-token>"
$env:GITHUB_TOKEN = "<github-pat-with-repo-read>"

Commands use \ to continue lines. In PowerShell, end the line with a backtick instead.

Steps

Prep (days before the cutover)

1. Run preflight

Catch bad tokens and unreachable orgs before you touch anything. doctor is read-only.

circleci-migrate doctor --source-org "$SOURCE_ORG" --dest-org "$DEST_ORG"

Check: it exits 0 with no hard failures.

2. Export the source

Export records names and structure, never secret values, and is read-only. Run it while the GitHub App is still installed on the source, so existing App pipelines are captured.

circleci-migrate export --source-org "$SOURCE_ORG" --dest-org "$DEST_ORG" \
 --output manifest.json --report migration-report.md

If you use self-hosted runners or publish orbs, add --runner-namespace <namespace> and --orb-namespace <namespace>.

Check: read migration-report.md in full and note the counts of contexts, projects and project env vars.

3. Write mapping.json

The mapping tells sync which org to write to. The org line is all you need, because App projects are matched by name.

cat > mapping.json <<EOF
{ "org": { "from": "$SOURCE_ORG", "to": "$DEST_ORG" } }
EOF
@{ org = @{ from = $SOURCE_ORG; to = $DEST_ORG } } | ConvertTo-Json | Set-Content mapping.json

If the repos also move to a new GitHub org, add "github_org": { "from": "acme", "to": "acme-new" } to the file and pass --dest-github-org acme-new to every sync below. See mapping.

Check: mapping.json has org.to set to the destination.

4. Create the migration-secrets context

Secret values can only be read inside a pipeline. The transfer pipeline runs in the source org and gets the destination token from a context. In the source org, go to Organization Settings > Contexts and create migration-secrets with one variable, CIRCLECI_DEST_TOKEN, set to the destination token.

Check: the context exists in the source org with that one variable.

5. Ask CircleCI support to plan the moves

The plan, and any same-name orb namespace, cannot move through the API. Tell support the destination org ID and the date you will move the GitHub App. The destination org must be on the Free plan and not share another org's plan.

Check: support confirms they will run it after the App moves.

6. Dry-run the cutover commands

Every command below is a dry run until you add --apply. Read each plan now.

circleci-migrate sync --manifest manifest.json --mapping mapping.json --skip-pipelines --skip-orb --skip-runner
circleci-migrate secrets transfer --manifest manifest.json --mapping mapping.json \
 --dest-org-id "$DEST_ORG_ID" --dest-token-context migration-secrets \
 --include-project-vars --include-ssh-keys --remove-restrictions
circleci-migrate cutover --manifest manifest.json --mapping mapping.json --pause-source

Check: no unexplained error lines. Every project shows SKIP in the transfer plan because the destination projects do not exist yet. That is expected.

Cutover (inside the freeze window)

7. Freeze merges and create the destination projects

Stop merges in the source repos (branch protection, a merge freeze, or an announcement) so nothing lands between the transfer and the switch. Then create the projects: project env vars are written into them, so they must exist first. This creates projects, contexts and settings, but no pipelines or triggers, and needs no GitHub token.

circleci-migrate sync --manifest manifest.json --mapping mapping.json \
 --skip-pipelines --skip-orb --skip-runner --apply

Check: every project reports skipped: --skip-pipelines, and the team confirms the freeze. Re-run the step 6 transfer dry run: no project shows SKIP now.

8. Transfer the secrets

This runs one pipeline per source project and writes each value straight to the destination over TLS. Nothing touches disk. It must run before you pause the source, because a paused project drops the pipeline.

circleci-migrate secrets transfer --manifest manifest.json --mapping mapping.json \
 --dest-org-id "$DEST_ORG_ID" --dest-token-context migration-secrets \
 --include-project-vars --include-ssh-keys --remove-restrictions \
 --enable-trigger --apply

Check: the log reports every context and project pipeline succeeded. See secrets.

9. Pause the source

Pausing stops builds in the source and records every change in cutover-state.json, so you can undo it. Preview first.

circleci-migrate cutover --manifest manifest.json --mapping mapping.json --pause-source
circleci-migrate cutover --manifest manifest.json --mapping mapping.json --pause-source --apply

Check: every source project is listed as paused, and cutover-state.json exists. Keep it until the cutover is confirmed.

10. Move the GitHub App

A GitHub org connects to one CircleCI org at a time. Uninstall the CircleCI GitHub App from the source org's connection. Then install it from the destination org on the same GitHub org, with every migrating repo selected. Each user opens the new org and clicks Authorize, then Refresh permissions if Projects is empty.

Caution

Point of no return. Uninstalling deletes the source org's GitHub App pipelines and triggers, and the export is the only record of them. cutover --undo can no longer re-enable them.

Now ask CircleCI support to move the plan to the destination org, and carry on while they work.

Check: the destination org lists every repo as connected, and support confirms the plan request. A repo that is not connected still gets a project, but its definition is created only after you connect it and re-run sync in the next step.

11. Add pipeline definitions and triggers

The App is connected, so definitions can be created. Triggers are created disabled. New webhook URLs and secrets go to webhook-secrets.json (mode 0600).

circleci-migrate sync --manifest manifest.json --mapping mapping.json \
 --skip-orb --skip-runner --apply --webhook-secrets-out webhook-secrets.json

Answer N at the "Enable N trigger(s)" prompt. cutover enables them in step 13.

Check: no line says "connect the repo to the GitHub App". If one does, connect the repo and re-run.

12. Move orbs and runners (only if you use them)

A namespace belongs to one org. Support moves a same-name namespace, and orb references need no change. For a different namespace, republish and rewrite your orb references. Resource classes are recreated, but runner instances never move, so register agents with new tokens. After a namespace move the classes stay attributed to the source: delete the copies, re-run this sync, then issue new tokens.

circleci-migrate sync --manifest manifest.json --mapping mapping.json \
 --only orb --dest-orb-namespace <new-namespace> --apply
circleci-migrate sync --manifest manifest.json --mapping mapping.json \
 --only runner --dest-runner-namespace <namespace> --apply

Check: runners show online in the destination, and validate lists the orbs (see Verify).

13. Enable the destination

This enables only the triggers that were enabled in the source. Do not run sync --apply --yes here: it enables triggers without pausing the source, so both orgs build.

circleci-migrate cutover --manifest manifest.json --mapping mapping.json --enable-dest
circleci-migrate cutover --manifest manifest.json --mapping mapping.json --enable-dest --apply

Check: no project reports manual. If one does, enable that trigger in Project Settings > Triggers. See cutover.

Verify

Push a commit to a migrated repo. Check: a pipeline starts in the destination org, runs green, and a job can read a context variable.

circleci-migrate validate --source-org "$SOURCE_ORG" --dest-org "$DEST_ORG" \
 --mapping mapping.json --dest-token-context migration-secrets

A clean report exits 0 and lists only expected manual items: group context restrictions, SSO and role bindings. Add --dest-runner-namespace and --dest-orb-namespace to compare runners and orbs. Then clean up:

  • Give each webhook sender and receiver its new value from webhook-secrets.json, then delete the file (it holds credentials; re-runs merge into it).
  • Rotate every transferred secret. Revoke the destination token and delete the migration-secrets context.
  • Update cloud OIDC trust policies for the new org ID and any IP allowlists. New SSO users default to Viewer: set Contributor for people who trigger pipelines.
  • Update service catalogs, badges, Slack apps and required status checks for the new project slugs.

Roll back

Before step 10, undo everything: this restores the source flags and triggers and disables the destination triggers it enabled.

circleci-migrate cutover --manifest manifest.json --mapping mapping.json --undo --apply

After step 10, --undo restores only the drop-all-build-requests flag. It does not move the GitHub App. To return, uninstall the App from the destination org and reinstall it from the source.

If something fails

Error Fix
the project has no SSH key The project has no GitHub App pipeline or checkout key. Add a deploy key in Project Settings > SSH Keys and re-run step 8. Run it before step 10 and this rarely happens.
source project(s) are paused Run the transfer before the pause, or run cutover --undo --apply and retry.
Empty Projects page for a user The user has not authorized yet. Authorize, then Refresh permissions.

More in troubleshooting. Flags: sync, secrets transfer, cutover.

item.title: GitHub OAuth to GitHub OAuth
item.description:
Use this runbook to move one OAuth org (gh/… or bb/…) to another OAuth org: a rename, a consolidation, or a move to a new GitHub org. Do the prep ahead of time, then run the cutover inside a freeze window.

At a glance 

flowchart LR
subgraph prep ["Prep (days before)"]
direction TB
A["Doctor, export,<br/>mapping"] --> B["Create contexts and<br/>projects (paused)"]
end
subgraph cut ["Cutover"]
direction TB
C["Freeze merges"] --> D["Transfer secrets"] --> E["Pause source"]
end
prep --> cut --> F["Enable destination<br/>SWITCH POINT"] --> G["Smoke test,<br/>validate"]
classDef sw fill:#8a6100,stroke:#5c4100,stroke-width:2px,color:#fff
class F sw

There is no point of no return. The source is only paused, never changed or deleted, and cutover --undo puts it back.

What moves

Moves Needs a step Does not move
Contexts, projects, project and org settings, schedules Secret values and SSH keys (secrets transfer) Group context restrictions
Project and expression context restrictions Webhook secrets and URLs (new ones are generated) SSO, build history, Insights
Self-hosted runner resource classes Orbs, runner instances (see steps 11 and 12) Per-project role grants

The full list is in what moves.

Before you start

  • You are an admin of both CircleCI orgs, and the destination org already exists.
  • Two personal API tokens (User Settings > Personal API Tokens), one per org.
  • The CLI is installed (install). circleci-migrate version prints v0.19.0 or later.
  • Every source project has a checkout key (Project Settings > SSH Keys) or a GitHub App pipeline. The transfer pipeline needs one of them.
  • Repos moving to a new GitHub org: a GitHub token with repo read, and the secrets transfer scheduled before the repos move (step 8).
  • A freeze window agreed with the team.

Set up 

export SOURCE_ORG="gh/acme"
export DEST_ORG="gh/acme-new"
export DEST_ORG_ID="<dest-org-uuid>"
export CIRCLECI_SOURCE_TOKEN="<source-org-admin-token>"
export CIRCLECI_DEST_TOKEN="<destination-org-admin-token>"
export GITHUB_TOKEN="<github-pat-with-repo-read>" # only if repos move to a new GitHub org
$SOURCE_ORG = "gh/acme"
$DEST_ORG = "gh/acme-new"
$DEST_ORG_ID = "<dest-org-uuid>"
$env:CIRCLECI_SOURCE_TOKEN = "<source-org-admin-token>"
$env:CIRCLECI_DEST_TOKEN = "<destination-org-admin-token>"
$env:GITHUB_TOKEN = "<github-pat-with-repo-read>" # only if repos move to a new GitHub org

The destination org ID is under Organization Settings > Overview. Commands use \ to continue lines. In PowerShell, end the line with a backtick instead.

Tip

Prefer prompts? circleci-migrate migrate runs export, sync, secrets transfer and validation in one guided pass. This runbook is the same flow with a pause between each step.

Steps

Prep

1. Run preflight

Catch bad tokens and unreachable orgs early. doctor is read-only.

circleci-migrate doctor --source-org "$SOURCE_ORG" --dest-org "$DEST_ORG"

Check: it exits 0 with no hard failures.

2. Export the source

Export records names and structure, never secret values, and is read-only.

circleci-migrate export --source-org "$SOURCE_ORG" --output manifest.json --report migration-report.md

Add --runner-namespace <namespace> for self-hosted runners and --orb-namespace <namespace> for orbs. Repos that were never followed in CircleCI are missing from the export. Add --follow-all (needs GITHUB_TOKEN) to follow them first.

Check: read migration-report.md in full and note the counts of contexts, projects and project env vars.

3. Write mapping.json

Without org.to, sync writes to your source org. The mapping prevents that.

cat > mapping.json <<EOF
{ "org": { "from": "$SOURCE_ORG", "to": "$DEST_ORG" } }
EOF
@{ org = @{ from = $SOURCE_ORG; to = $DEST_ORG } } | ConvertTo-Json | Set-Content mapping.json

If the repos moved to a new GitHub org, also add "github_org": { "from": "acme", "to": "acme-new" }. See mapping.

Check: mapping.json has org.to set to the destination.

4. Create the migration-secrets context

Secret values can only be read inside a pipeline. The transfer pipeline runs in the source org and gets the destination token from a context. In the source org, go to Organization Settings > Contexts and create migration-secrets with one variable, CIRCLECI_DEST_TOKEN, set to the destination token.

Check: the context exists in the source org with that one variable.

5. Dry-run the sync

Without --apply, nothing is written. Read the plan before you apply.

circleci-migrate sync --manifest manifest.json --mapping mapping.json

Check: no unexpected error lines. manual lines for secret values are expected, because those move in step 8. Project counts match the report.

Cutover

6. Create the destination contexts and projects

This creates contexts, projects, settings, webhooks and schedules in the destination. OAuth projects are created paused: no webhook, no builds.

circleci-migrate sync --manifest manifest.json --mapping mapping.json \
 --apply --webhook-secrets-out webhook-secrets.json

Answer N at the "Enable builds" prompt. For repos in a new GitHub org, add --dest-github-org acme-new.

Check: re-run step 5. Every line now says exists.

7. Match source projects to destination projects

Secret transfer routes project values by slug, and OAuth slugs need an explicit entry per project. This overwrites mapping.json, so re-add any github_org line afterwards. It needs the destination token.

circleci-migrate mapping generate --manifest manifest.json --dest-org "$DEST_ORG" --output mapping.json

Check: the report lists each source project under matched, with none unmatched.

8. Freeze merges, then transfer the secrets

Freeze merges in the source repos so the values you copy are the final ones. The transfer runs one pipeline per source project and writes each value straight to the destination over TLS. Nothing touches disk. If your repos move to a new GitHub org, run it before they move, because the pipelines check out code from the old org.

circleci-migrate secrets transfer --manifest manifest.json --mapping mapping.json \
 --dest-org-id "$DEST_ORG_ID" --dest-token-context migration-secrets \
 --include-project-vars --include-ssh-keys --remove-restrictions --enable-trigger
circleci-migrate secrets transfer --manifest manifest.json --mapping mapping.json \
 --dest-org-id "$DEST_ORG_ID" --dest-token-context migration-secrets \
 --include-project-vars --include-ssh-keys --remove-restrictions --enable-trigger --apply

Check: the dry run lists no SKIP. The apply reports every pipeline succeeded. See secrets.

9. Pause the source

Pausing stops new builds in the source so both orgs never build the same push. Every change is recorded in cutover-state.json, so you can undo it.

circleci-migrate cutover --manifest manifest.json --mapping mapping.json --pause-source
circleci-migrate cutover --manifest manifest.json --mapping mapping.json --pause-source --apply

Add --pause-org to pause the whole source org. Keep cutover-state.json until you confirm the cutover.

Check: every source project is listed as paused. See cutover.

10. Enable the destination

Following each project installs the GitHub webhook and deploy key, so pushes start building in the destination. --yes skips the confirmation prompt. cutover --enable-dest does nothing for an OAuth destination, which is why the source is paused with cutover --pause-source in the step before.

circleci-migrate sync --manifest manifest.json --mapping mapping.json --apply --yes

Check: the destination Projects page shows every project as followed.

11. Move orbs (only if you publish orbs)

A namespace belongs to one org. Ask CircleCI support to move a same-name namespace, and orb references need no change. To publish under a different namespace instead, run:

circleci-migrate sync --manifest manifest.json --mapping mapping.json \
 --only orb --dest-orb-namespace <new-namespace> --apply

Check: the orbs are listed by validate (see Verify). If you used a new namespace, rewrite the orb references in your configs.

12. Recreate runners (only if you use them)

Resource classes are recreated, but runner instances never move. Register agents with new tokens.

circleci-migrate sync --manifest manifest.json --mapping mapping.json \
 --only runner --dest-runner-namespace <namespace> --apply

Check: runners register against the destination classes and show online.

Verify

Push a commit to a migrated repo. Check: a pipeline starts in the destination org, runs green, and a job can read a context variable.

circleci-migrate validate --source-org "$SOURCE_ORG" --dest-org "$DEST_ORG" \
 --mapping mapping.json --dest-token-context migration-secrets

A clean report exits 0 and lists only expected manual items: group context restrictions, SSO and role bindings. Add --dest-runner-namespace and --dest-orb-namespace to compare runners and orbs.

Then clean up:

  • Give each webhook sender and receiver its new value from webhook-secrets.json, then delete the file.
  • Recreate group context restrictions in the destination UI.
  • Rotate every transferred secret. Rotate the destination token and delete the migration-secrets context.
  • If the source had drop_all_build_requests or require_context_group_restriction on, set them now with sync --include-danger-flags --apply.
  • Update badges, Slack apps and required status checks to the new org.

Roll back

Undo restores the source flags and re-enables the source triggers it disabled.

circleci-migrate cutover --manifest manifest.json --mapping mapping.json --undo --apply

--undo does not unfollow destination projects. To stop destination builds, unfollow the projects in the destination UI. The source org itself is never deleted or altered beyond the pause.

If something fails

Error Fix
the project has no SSH key The source project has no checkout key or GitHub App pipeline. Add a deploy key in Project Settings > SSH Keys and re-run step 8.
source project(s) are paused Run the transfer before the pause, or run cutover --undo --apply and retry.
SKIP for a project in the transfer plan No destination project matches. Re-run steps 6 and 7.
sync wrote to the source org mapping.json has no org.to. Fix it and re-run.
No pipeline after the push Confirm the project is followed and the GitHub webhook is installed.
validate shows the migration-secrets context missing Pass --dest-token-context migration-secrets.

More in troubleshooting. Flags: sync, secrets transfer, cutover.

item.title: GitHub App to GitHub App
item.description:
Use this runbook to move one GitHub App or standalone org (circleci/…) to another (circleci/…): a consolidation, a split, or a move to a new GitHub org. Do the prep ahead of time, then run the cutover inside a freeze window.

subgraph prep ["Prep (days before)"]
direction TB

end
subgraph before ["Cutover: source still live"]
direction TB

end

direction TB
H["Add pipelines<br/>and triggers"] --> I["Enable destination"] --> J["Smoke test, validate"]

Check: the log reports every context and project pipeline succeeded. See secrets.

8. Pause the source

Pausing stops builds in the source and records every change in cutover-state.json, so you can undo it. Preview first.

circleci-migrate cutover --manifest manifest.json --mapping mapping.json --pause-source
circleci-migrate cutover --manifest manifest.json --mapping mapping.json --pause-source --apply

Check: every source project is listed as paused, and cutover-state.json exists. Keep it until the cutover is confirmed.

9. Connect the repos to the destination

Definitions can only be created for repos the destination GitHub App can see.

  • New GitHub org: confirm every repo is connected in the destination org's GitHub App installation. Nothing is uninstalled.
  • Same GitHub org: uninstall the CircleCI GitHub App from the source org's connection, then install it from the destination org with every migrating repo selected. Users click Authorize, then Refresh permissions if Projects is empty.

Caution

Same GitHub org only. Uninstalling deletes the source org's GitHub App pipelines and triggers, and the export is the only record of them. cutover --undo can no longer re-enable them.

Check: the destination org lists every repo as connected.

Tip

New GitHub org only: if you created definitions and triggers earlier (a sync --apply without --skip-pipelines), the pause and the enable can run as one command: cutover --pause-source --enable-dest --apply. Run the transfer first.

10. Add pipeline definitions and triggers

Triggers are created disabled. New webhook URLs and secrets go to webhook-secrets.json (mode 0600). Answer N at the "Enable N trigger(s)" prompt, because cutover enables them in step 12.

circleci-migrate sync --manifest manifest.json --mapping mapping.json \
 --skip-orb --skip-runner --apply --webhook-secrets-out webhook-secrets.json

Check: no line says "connect the repo to the GitHub App". If one does, connect the repo and re-run.

11. Move orbs and runners (only if you use them)

A namespace belongs to one org. Ask CircleCI support to move a same-name namespace, and orb references need no change. For a different namespace, republish. Resource classes are recreated, but runner instances never move, so register agents with new tokens.

circleci-migrate sync --manifest manifest.json --mapping mapping.json \
 --only orb --dest-orb-namespace <new-namespace> --apply
circleci-migrate sync --manifest manifest.json --mapping mapping.json \
 --only runner --dest-runner-namespace <namespace> --apply

Check: runners show online, and validate lists the orbs (see Verify). Update cloud OIDC trust policies for the new org ID.

12. Enable the destination

This enables only the triggers that were enabled in the source. Do not run sync --apply --yes here: it enables triggers without pausing the source, so both orgs build.

circleci-migrate cutover --manifest manifest.json --mapping mapping.json --enable-dest
circleci-migrate cutover --manifest manifest.json --mapping mapping.json --enable-dest --apply

Check: no project reports manual. If one does, enable that trigger in Project Settings > Triggers. See cutover.

Verify

Push a commit to a migrated repo. Check: a pipeline starts in the destination org, runs green, and a job can read a context variable.

circleci-migrate validate --source-org "$SOURCE_ORG" --dest-org "$DEST_ORG" \
 --mapping mapping.json --dest-token-context migration-secrets

A clean report exits 0 and lists only expected manual items: SSO, role bindings and per-project grants. Add --dest-runner-namespace and --dest-orb-namespace to compare runners and orbs. Then clean up:

  • Give each webhook sender and receiver its new value from webhook-secrets.json, then delete the file.
  • Recreate per-project role grants in the destination.
  • Rotate every transferred secret. Rotate the destination token and delete the migration-secrets context.
  • Update badges, Slack apps and required status checks for the new project slugs.

Roll back

Before the App moves in step 9, undo everything. This restores the source flags and triggers and disables the destination triggers it enabled.

circleci-migrate cutover --manifest manifest.json --mapping mapping.json --undo --apply

After a same-GitHub-org App move, --undo restores only the drop-all-build-requests flag. It does not move the App. To return, uninstall it from the destination org and reinstall it from the source.

If your org is mixed (OAuth and App)

When one GitHub org has both integrations, CircleCI keeps two org records: gh/<org> and circleci/<id>. Migrate each as its own leg, with its own manifest, mapping and state file.

  • OAuth leg: follow OAuth to GitHub App, or OAuth to OAuth if the destination is OAuth.
  • App leg: follow this runbook. Add --skip-org-settings to its sync commands if the first leg already wrote the org settings, and --state cutover-state-app.json to every cutover command.

If something fails

Error Fix
Pipeline definition is manual: connect the repo Connect the repo to the destination GitHub App and re-run sync --apply.
source project(s) are paused Run the transfer before the pause, or run cutover --undo --apply and retry.
Org roles missing in the destination The user is not yet a destination member. Add them, then re-run sync --apply.
Wrong repo IDs after a GitHub org move Set GITHUB_TOKEN and pass --dest-github-org to sync.
